credit.altimetry: Altimetry data are provided by NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry.
credit.gauges: Permanent Service for Mean Sea Level (PSMSL), Revised Local Reference annual means.

gauges.name: Brest
gauges.why: One of the longest instrumental records of anything, from 1807.

gauges.name: New York
gauges.why: The Battery, from 1856. The mid-Atlantic coast is subsiding, so it reads faster than the global mean.

gauges.name: San Francisco
gauges.why: From 1855, and close to the global average.

gauges.name: Honolulu
gauges.why: Mid-ocean, far from any subsiding delta, which makes it the nearest thing to a global reading a single gauge gives.

gauges.name: Galveston
gauges.why: Fast rise, and most of it is the ground going down after a century of oil, gas and groundwater extraction.

gauges.name: Manila
gauges.why: The fastest rise in this set, several times the global mean, almost all of it groundwater subsidence rather than ocean.

gauges.name: Stockholm
gauges.why: Sea level FALLING, because Scandinavia is still rebounding from the ice sheet that left ten thousand years ago.

gauges.name: Oslo
gauges.why: Also falling, for the same reason as Stockholm.

gauges.name: Skagway
gauges.why: Falling faster than anywhere else on Earth: the land is rising about two centimetres a year as Little Ice Age glaciers unload it.

gauges.name: Sydney
gauges.why: Fort Denison, the southern hemisphere's long record.
